facts.raw_span: a crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region
irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
no significant past medical history
laboratory studies were unremarkable
lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
no clear evidence of basaloid nests
invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
focal area of uptake in the supraorbital lesion (SUVmax 6.9; metabolic tumor volume, 2 cc)
the plaque had regressed markedly
several discrete papular lesions remained
features typical of basal cell carcinoma
decreased uptake in the original lesion (SUVmax 4.8; metabolic tumor volume, 0.5 cc)

aliases: squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
concepts.why: The patient's biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis, consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
Dermoscopic evaluation of the papules revealed features typical of basal cell carcinoma.

rationales.F05: Eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The diagnosis of invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma was directly stated.
rationales.F11: The presence of features typical of basal cell carcinoma suggests this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The biopsy results and initial PET/CT findings strongly support invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, while the later appearance of basal cell carcinoma features suggests a possible second primary tumor.
